findings.title: Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian account messages (totpStep1)
findings.body: The change to `totpStep1` replaced the old Lithuanian sentence (which contained outdated anchor links) with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" — that is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will now see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page of the account console. The correct replacement should be a Lithuanian translation of the current English source ("Install one of the following applications on your mobile:"), as was done correctly for the fi, sk, sv and no bundles in this same PR.

findings.title: Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian login messages (loginTotpStep1)
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1` was changed from a Lithuanian sentence to "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the mobile authenticator setup step of the login flow. This should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:" (compare with the correct Slovak, Swedish, Finnish and Norwegian replacements made in this PR).

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text introduced into the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle
findings.body: The new value `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) in the Simplified Chinese `zh_CN` bundle. The rest of this file (and the zh_CN login bundle, which uses 在您的移动设备中安装以下任意一个应用) is Simplified Chinese, so users get an inconsistent script variant. It should read e.g. "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：".

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched to Java MessageFormat choice syntax that the i18next-based admin console cannot render
findings.body: This key was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The keycloak.v2 admin console formats these messages client-side with react-i18next, whose interpolation syntax is `{{0}}` (which is why the previous value used it) and which has no support for Java's `{2,choice,...}` clause. When this error is displayed for a multivalued attribute validation failure, the console will show the raw pattern text instead of substituting the attribute name and bounds. The server-side bundles (themes/.../admin and themes/.../login messages_en.properties) can use this syntax because they are formatted with java.text.MessageFormat, but the React console bundles must keep `{{0}}`-style placeholders.

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched to Java MessageFormat choice syntax that the i18next-based account console cannot render
findings.body: This key was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The keycloak.v3 account console renders these messages with i18next (`{{0}}` interpolation, as used by the previous version of this key), and vanilla i18next cannot evaluate a Java `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` expression — the choice clause will be displayed literally and the `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` placeholders won't follow this file's interpolation convention. Users hitting this validation error will see the raw format string instead of a readable message.

findings.title: Anchor validation requires identical anchors in identical order and stops at the first mismatch
findings.body: In `santizeAnchors` the n-th anchor found in the translation is compared with the n-th anchor found in the English source using sequential `find()` calls. A translation that contains exactly the same anchors as the source but in a different order — legitimate when grammar or right-to-left mirroring reorders links in a sentence — is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" and fails the build. Additionally the `break` after the first mismatch means any further anchors in the same value are never validated. Comparing against the multiset/list of English anchors (membership instead of positional matching) would avoid these false positives.

findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws bare RuntimeException when a properties file can't be read, bypassing the MojoExecutionException contract
findings.body: `verify()` declares `MojoExecutionException` and converts IO failures of the primary file read into it, but the new `verifySafeHtml()` opens the target file and the derived English file again and throws plain `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")` on failure (also at line 70). This happens, for example, when a community locale file has no English counterpart under `resources/`, so adding a new translation can crash the Maven plugin with an internal-error stack trace instead of a clean, file-named plugin error or a regular verification message. These exceptions should be wrapped in `MojoExecutionException` (or reported as verification messages) for consistent error reporting.
